0.long_answer: The epidemic disease that emerged in November 2002 and was characterized by symptoms such as lymphocytopenia is severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS). SARS is an infectious disease caused by a coronavirus, and its outbreak rapidly spread across multiple countries, affecting thousands of individuals. One of its hallmark features in patients was lymphopenia, a notable reduction in lymphocyte counts, which was observed in many affected individuals. This outbreak, starting in November 2002, eventually led to a global public health response as the disease spread across continents before it was brought under control.
